page: Microsoft Azure D8lds_v6 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Dldsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. This instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes a 472 GB local storage disk and supports Premium Storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2166.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.52 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is moderate, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 8360.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 7990.55. Memory bandwidth is measured at 621.35 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 67.27 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. For machine learning workloads, the server achieves a strong text generation speed of 313.4 tokens/sec on a small 135M LLM, but drops to a weak 7.97 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D8lds_v6 offers a resource-dense compute profile. By constraining system memory to 16.0 GB, it reduces overhead costs for workloads that are CPU-bound rather than memory-bound. However, the 2.0 GB per core memory limit represents a clear tradeoff, rendering the instance unsuitable for large-scale in-memory databases or heavy multi-threaded LLM inference. Appropriate workloads include web serving, software compilation, text processing, and lightweight database operations.
